chunks: So that (men) may believe in God and His Apostle, and honour Him and revere Him, and sing His praises morning and evening.
ai.seo_question: What is the purpose of believing in God and His Messenger according to Surah Al-Fath?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Fath (48:9) is often linked to the event of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, highlighting how divine guidance aims to strengthen the community's spiritual resolve. It emphasizes not just belief, but active glorification (tubaddir) and reverence (tuwaqqir) of Allah and the Prophet, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the interconnection of faith, love, and honor for the Ahl al-Bayt. The continuous glorification 'morning and evening' underscores the perpetual state of mindfulness required of the faithful.
